claims.claim: **CNS, respiratory and cardiac effects are the main concern.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Inhalation injury may appear up to 6 hours after exposure.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **In children, under 5 mL of undiluted essential oil can produce significant CNS toxicity.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hydrocarbons can produce seizures and CNS depression of rapid onset**; aspiration of volatile ones leads to **chemical pneumonitis**. Dysrhythmias are less common.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Exposure is accidental (often younger children) or deliberate (often inhaled — 'sniffing' or 'chroming').**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Sources:** kerosene, petrol, paraffin oil, lighter fluid, diesel, 2-stroke fuel, white spirit, solvents, furniture polishes, lubricating oil, mineral turpentine, essential oils.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Assess:** any symptomatic child · every significant accidental exposure or deliberate self-poisoning · any child whose developmental age does not fit accidental poisoning.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **History:** intent · type of compound · quantity ingested · duration of any inhalation · co-ingestants such as paracetamol.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Coughing, gagging or choking means aspiration.** Evolving chemical pneumonitis shows as wheeze, hypoxia, tachypnoea, haemoptysis and pulmonary oedema.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Dysrhythmias occur early.** CNS depression, coma and seizures may follow large acute exposures, **usually within 2 hours.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Asymptomatic child, small ingestion: usually no investigation.** Significant ingestion or symptoms: **12-lead ECG and 4 hours of cardiac monitoring**, VBG, FBE, UEC, LFTs, and CXR if respiratory symptoms.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Deliberate poisoning:** screen for co-ingestants — BSL and paracetamol level.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Care is supportive; if CNS depression is progressing, intubate early.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Ventricular dysrhythmias:** advanced life support · intubate, hyperventilate and correct hypoxia · correct electrolytes · **withhold catecholamine inotropes if possible.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Seizures: benzodiazepines first line; avoid phenytoin.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Chemical pneumonitis is managed supportively** (oxygen, bronchodilators, NIV or intubation if severe). **No corticosteroids or prophylactic antibiotics**; fever is common after aspiration, so **antibiotics wait until bacterial infection is objectively shown.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Activated charcoal is specifically contraindicated:** it does not bind hydrocarbons and increases aspiration risk.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Asymptomatic with normal vital signs: observe 6 hours after exposure before discharge.** Milder respiratory or CNS symptoms: admit for longer observation ± supportive care.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider admission for all adolescents with an intentional overdose.** Poisons Information: 13 11 26.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **CNS depression, seizures or dysrhythmia → paediatric intensive care.** PIPER: 1300 137 650.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge criteria:** normal GCS · normal ECG · no cough, dyspnoea or wheeze · normal observations including oximetry · observation period complete · after deliberate ingestion, low assessed risk of further self-harm.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrocarbon poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrocarbon_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23
